Priya S.: FYI customer Lina (Acme) is seeing 429s + sudden latency spikes during bursts. Says it started after a traffic spike this morning. Paste of errors below.

Lina (Customer): sending a bit more detail — their pattern is a short burst of ~120 concurrent requests for ~20s every 5m. Most requests are text-generation with seq_len ~512. Getting 429 + long tails (~2-6s) then success. They suspect throttling.

Priya S.: Here are the headers Lina captured on failures: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 100
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 167
x-redwood-burst-remaining: 0
x-request-id: req_01F4
```

Samir (Infra): thanks. That x-redwood-burst-remaining is from our burst allocator. Means they exhausted burst credits for their API key. But the long tails are interesting — could be queue buildup on continuous-batching.

Alex K.: couple possibilities: 1) quota exhaustion -> 429s, 2) continuous batch queueing causing perceived throttling (requests enqueued waiting for batch), 3) KV cache cold/warm causing variable latency.

Priya S.: customer asks why they see 6s p99 then a 429 a few seconds later.

Samir (Infra): if the burst bucket empties mid-surge our routing will start rate-limiting new requests. Existing requests may stay queued until batch timeout then run; that explains some long tails. If their concurrency spikes fast we may be batching many short-lived requests into fewer large batches and kernel swapping can add tail latency.

Alex K.: quick repro steps for eng to reproduce: 
1) simulate 120 concurrent clients hitting /v1/generate with seq_len=512, prompt ~200 tokens, stream=false
2) set per-key QPS to match customer account (we have their key usage)
3) ramp in <5s, sustain 20s, repeat every 5m

Priya S.: attached sample curl they used: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1.0","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":256}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Support Bot: Incident note saved to #support-incidents (inc_2026-03-15-98). :white_check_mark:

quota-bot: Account acme-prod: monthly token quota 500M, used 42%. Burst credits remaining: 0 (refill in 2h).

Samir (Infra): their burst credits are 0 so subsequent requests will hit 429s. But we should still avoid long tails by reducing batch wait. What are their batching defaults?

Alex K.: default continuous-batching config: max_batch_size=64, max_batch_delay_ms=50, max_concurrency_per_worker=8. For 120 concurrent requests we can end up with 2-3 workers saturating and some requests queued on accept queue. If batches grow to 64 with seq_len 512 execution time ~300-400ms per batch, plus queue adds seconds under contention.

Priya S.: customer wants mitigation now — they asked: 1) why did we consume burst so fast? 2) how to avoid 429s + long tails? 3) any quick config changes?

Alex K.: answers: 1) burst is consumed when they exceed sustained commit; a sudden spike uses credits. 2) To avoid 429s: reduce concurrency, smooth bursts, or upgrade to Dedicated/raise quota. Also implement client-side retry with jitter and honor Retry-After header. 3) Quick server-side tweaks: lower max_batch_delay_ms to 10-20ms for that key (reduces queueing at cost of lower GPU throughput), or enable per-route smaller max_batch_size.

Samir (Infra): additional: warm KV cache before burst. If KV cache cold, first requests pay extra time for KV fill which can slow batch completion. Recommend pre-warming with a small warmup burst (low QPS) right before planned traffic. For unknown traffic, use prefix caching or set cache TTL longer on common prefixes.

Priya S.: Lina — proposed immediate mitigations: 
- set client retry with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After (we can share sample)
- temporarily reduce concurrency (throttle on client side) to keep within quota until burst credits refill
- if acceptable, enable a per-key override to reduce max_batch_delay_ms to 20ms for 2 hours (ops can do).

Lina (Customer): could we get the ops override? Our traffic pattern is bursty from user events, hard to smooth in-app quickly.

Samir (Infra): I can apply a temporary override per-key for batch_delay and max_batch_size. Will need approval from infra lead. Alex, any objections to 20ms / max_batch_size=32 for 2h?

Alex K.: 20ms + size 32 should reduce tail latency significantly for this workload. Throughput will drop ~15-25% but acceptable short term. Also recommend they enable streaming responses if they can — reduces perceived latency for users.

Priya S.: action items: 
- Samir to request override (in progress)
- Lina to implement client-side retries + lower concurrency (we'll send sample)
- Alex to provide short doc on batch_delay tradeoffs and KV warm strategies

Samir (Infra): override request sent to infra-lead. Ticket INF-2227. ETA ~30m.

Support Bot: INF-2227 approved by @jordan (Infra Lead) :tada:

Samir (Infra): override applied: per-key config: {"max_batch_delay_ms":"20","max_batch_size":"32"} for key acme-prod window 2h. Monitor logs.

Priya S.: Lina — please try to restart your burst and report p50/p95/p99 and any 429s. Also paste response headers if you still see 429.

Lina (Customer): restarting now. First 2 waves look much better, p95 dropped from ~2.8s to 0.9s. No 429s in first 2 waves. Will monitor during next refill window. Thank you! :heart:

Alex K.: notes for eng followup: add a diagnostic flag that logs per-request batch_id + queue_time + exec_time to make postmortem easier. Also consider per-key adaptive batch_delay based on observed queue_time.

Priya S.: marking resolved for now; will reopen if 429s return after burst credits refill. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
